newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end sharply lower, glued to Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end sharply lower, glued to Dow.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended sharply lower on Monday as local stock prices moved in tandem with U.S. stocks, which took a hit on rising long-bond yields, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most active shares closed off 2.45 percent at 9,044 points. Market turnover was lower than usual at 449.5 million reais ($424.05 million).
"It was all New York again," said a senior trader.
Analysts said the market absorbed well the takeover of troubled private bank Banco Bamerindus by HSBC Holdings Plc.

Banco HSBC Bamerindus SA, the new bank which emerged from the assumption of Bamerindus' selected assets and liabilities by HSBC, opened smoothly on Monday, with clients apparently confident about the bank's new administration.
Trading in Bamerindus, which was halted late on Wednesday, remained suspended today on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) even after the announcement of the takeover deal.
Bellwether Telebras preferred lost 2.58 percent, ending at 109.60 reais.
State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce preferred fell 2.82 percent to 24.70 reais,
State oil firm Petrobras preferred dropped 3.44 percent to 210.50 reais.
The power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most liquid stocks in the electrical sector, fell 1.51 percent, closing at 2,494 points.
